summary.intent: Autonomously plan, execute, and ship phase 63 (read-chain navigation and rotation core) — a crypto-heavy sdk-core phase covering IPNS-backed read-chain navigation, read grant issuance, and a rotation engine — while the user was AFK.
summary.outcome: All 7 plans executed across 4 waves with 25+ commits; verification passed (5/5 must-haves), security audit secured (27/27 threats closed), SDK-E2E gate passed against live stack, CodeRabbit review triaged. At transcript end the in-scope fixer agent was still applying CodeRabbit hygiene fixes before the PR would be opened.

repo: Repo squash-merges to main, so individual commit subjects never reach release-please. Only the PR title needs to be conventional and paren-free; rewording branch commits via filter-branch is unnecessary.

sdk-core has no `typecheck` script — the real type gate is `build` which runs `tsup && tsc -p tsconfig.build.json`. Plans 63-05 and 63-06 referenced a non-existent `typecheck` script and had to be redirected.

The §3.5 design spec for move-within-scope requires re-sealing the child readKey under the new parent's readKey (reseal + republish). The implemented `moveItem` is a pure synchronous link rewrite and does not re-seal, meaning a grantee navigating via the destination path would fail AAD authentication.
The GSD commit helper has a known false-negative pattern where it reports `commit_failed` even when the commit actually landed. Always verify with `git log --oneline -1` rather than retrying.

Worktree isolation is unsafe for this repo (node_modules leaks, api:generate side effects, tight cross-plan coupling on shared files like folder.test.ts). Sequential execution in the main tree is the correct default.
The Phase-62 D-01 quarantine left 89 intentionally skipped SDK-E2E tests across 11 suites with a note to re-enable at phases 63-65. This is expected and not a regression.
pr-release-preview.js parses individual commit types but the paren-rejection rule applies only to the PR title, not commit message descriptions.

code.finding: Uses `childRef.generation` (the parent-mirror value) rather than `childPublished.generation` — the critical generation-source rule that prevents spoofing.
`plainKey.fill(0)` called in both success path (L43) and catch path (L48), ensuring intermediate key material is always zeroed regardless of outcome.
Comment claimed zeroization happens in a `finally` block; actual implementation uses try/catch in rewrap.ts. Outcome is identical but the comment was inaccurate (fixed in this session).

PLACEHOLDER_WRITE_KEY (`new Uint8Array(32)`) passed as writeKey to `sealNode`. Safe in Phase 63 because the happy path never reaches a node with a writeBody, but latent risk if Phase 65+ hits this path before wiring the real key.
In the catch block, only `readKeyPrime.fill(0)` is called; `parentReadKey` is never zeroed (flagged by security audit as T-63-10 critical, mitigated).
Root `rotateOne` fires before the BFS frontier per §4.2 ordering requirement.
Anti-malicious-relay check: both the relay set AND `localGrantRecord` are cross-checked independently to prevent elevation of privilege (T-63-17).
Early returns `'no-rotation'` without calling `deps.rotate` when the item has no covering grant — the SC#4 zero-rotation invariant.
`sequenceNumber: 1n` embedded verbatim on first IPNS publish.
`publishWithCas` uses expected-sequence CAS guard to prevent concurrent write races (T-63-14).

Had 4 `describe.skip('...TODO(phase 63)')` blocks testing the retired `FolderChild`/`encryptFolderMetadata` API under `@ts-nocheck`. All confirmed superseded by new active blocks; removed in cleanup commit `6a739a20a`.

workflow: When a weekly API usage limit hits mid-subagent, the working tree remains clean if the subagent made atomic commits — no partial state to repair. Simply retry after reset.

Running the SDK-E2E gate during execution (plan 63-07) caught a real BFS bug in engine.ts: child `rotateOne` calls were receiving the root's new readKey instead of each child's own derived readKey. Unit suites with mocks would have missed this.

The GSD plan-checker should be re-run (iteration 2) after fixing its findings rather than skipping — it caught 1 blocker (RESEARCH.md open questions unmarked) and 2 warnings in iteration 1 that were all trivially fixable.
Drift gate (stale codebase map) is non-blocking at plan time when CONTEXT.md and RESEARCH.md carry precise, verified implementation-site references.
Security audit should be run in background in parallel with SDK-E2E gate and CodeRabbit to save wall-clock time during the ship pipeline.

CodeRabbit bundles findings by severity (critical/major/minor) in the review body; the correct triage split for a crypto phase is: hygiene fixes applied now, rotation-soundness and cross-phase concerns deferred as todos with file refs and destination phase.

friction: Weekly API usage limit hit during plan 63-06 executor mid-run at ~07:00 Berlin, causing a hard stop. The tree was clean (no partial work) so recovery was clean on retry after reset.
GSD commit helper false-negative pattern: reports `commit_failed` on every commit but the commit actually lands. Required verifying every commit via `git log --oneline -1` throughout the session.
Plans 63-05 and 63-06 referenced a non-existent `typecheck` script in sdk-core. Had to redirect to `build` at runtime.

4 stale `describe.skip(TODO(phase 63))` blocks in folder.test.ts were left by executors and required a dedicated cleanup subagent to safely remove (needed careful boundary analysis to avoid touching phase-65 blocks).
CodeRabbit returned 3 critical + 12 major + 5 minor findings requiring manual triage; most criticals/majors were in Phase-64 domain (rotation soundness) and had to be deferred rather than fixed.
The `gh pr edit` command is known to fail on this repo (Projects-classic GraphQL) — PR body must be patched via `gh api -X PATCH`.
